transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-30 16:00 UTC | Duration approx 52m | Attendees: Alex Stein (Redwood), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Gnosis Head of Search), Tom Alvarez (Platform), Sara Kim (Security), Ethan Park (Data Scientist)

Summary: initial discovery focused on embedding / rerank integration into Gnosis' existing search stack. Key constraints: on-prem vector DB (Milvus today), strict KMS + audit requirements, target 150 QPS peak for hybrid search, p95 end-to-end rerank <200-250ms. Evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments and tradeoffs around latency, cost, and data residency.

Topics: integration architecture, vector dims and quantization, hybrid fanout strategy, caching and batching, private/VPC connectivity, SOC2 & KMS, benchmarking plan, next steps.

00:00 Alex (Redwood): okay everyone thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros and then hop into the embedding and rerank flow you mentioned in the form.
00:18 Priya (Gnosis): hi yeah I'm Priya, I own search at Gnosis. We run a monolith search service with an ES layer plus Milvus for vectors, we want to add a neural reranker for topk refinement, that's the main ask.
00:30 Tom (Gnosis): tom here platform, curious about how much infra change we'll need. we have on-prem colo and some cloud for analytics.
00:39 Maya (Redwood): great, thanks. quick q on scale — what QPS and doc sizes are we talking?
00:45 Priya: bursts up to 150 QPS, steady 40-60 QPS. doc corpus ~12M docs, avg doc length 800 tokens; we do metadata filtering by tenant and region.
00:59 Ethan (Gnosis): our current embedding dims are 1536 from an older model; considering moving to 1024 or 768 to save storage and Fan-out cost.
01:10 Alex: cool. so three big choices: (1) host rerank in Redwood Hosted API (fast to get started), (2) Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, or (3) Redwood Private deployed in your VPC/on-prem for strict compliance. each has tradeoffs.
01:25 Sara (Gnosis): can we do private but still have Redwood manage rollout & updates? our compliance team wants customer-managed keys and audit logs.
01:33 Diego (Redwood): yes, Private supports KMS/HSM and audit log forwarding; you can choose customer-managed keys. there's some ops work for on-prem install but we provide an appliance and automation.
01:48 Priya: good. real question is latency — if we fanout to Milvus then call Redwood reranker as a second stage, what's realistic end-to-end p95?
01:59 Maya: depends on batch sizing, qps, and whether rerank runs on CPU or GPU. typical hosted rerank (GPU) for top-10 inputs is ~30-80ms per request for the model inference, add network & prep. with Dedicated we can reserve GPUs to keep tail stable; Private reduces cross-cloud network hops.
02:20 Tom: our network hops are the killer. Milvus is on-prem in the same colo as our ES nodes but Redwood Hosted is cloud — that extra hop worries us for tail latency.
02:32 Alex: that's the common tradeoff. two patterns we've seen: (A) keep vector store & search colocated, and run rerank in a Private instance in the same VPC/colo (best latency + encryption) or (B) use Hosted for model serving and put a small edge proxy close to Milvus to batch requests and reduce RTT.
02:50 Priya: what about hybrid search? we want lexical + vector and then rerank on the combined top-K. how do you handle scoring mismatches and rerank precision?
03:03 Maya: common approach is fanout-merge: get top-K from lexical and vector, unify by doc id with de-dupe, then run a reranker model on the merged list. For scale we recommend limiting rerank to top 100 and then final top-10 for UI. also caching the merged candidate set when queries repeat is helpful.
03:28 Ethan: our cost concern is embedding dims and storage. if we go from 1536 to 768, do we lose rerank quality?
03:36 Maya: there's a tradeoff. many teams use 768 or 1024 for retrieval and then run a small fine-tuned reranker model to recover rank quality. quantized embeddings (8-bit) reduce storage but can slightly change nearest-neighbor behavior, so you want to validate with your eval set.
03:50 Priya: okay, we need an eval — can Redwood run an A/B with different dims and rerank models?
03:58 Alex: yes, we can run a pilot: you'll provide an anonymized dataset and query set; SE team will run three configurations (1536 full, 1024, and quantized 768) and we measure recall@k and rerank latency/cost.
04:12 Tom: what about vector DB compatibility? we currently use Milvus but may consider vector engine migration later. any connectors?
04:20 Diego: we integrate via standard vector APIs and can work with Milvus, Faiss (self-host), Pinecone, and others. we also have a small client shim that keeps consistent ids and metadata across systems. for private deployments, we can deploy the rerank runtime inside your network so it talks locally to Milvus.
04:40 Sara: security — we need SOC2 + ISO 27001 and SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. also, we require per-tenant encryption keys for particularly sensitive research clients.
04:52 Alex: Redwood has SOC2 report and ISO in process; Private mode supports external KMS and per-tenant encryption. we'll share the compliance pack after the call.
05:01 Priya: another ops question: how do you handle caching / KV cache for rerank to reduce compute? we see many repeated queries.
05:10 Maya: we support prefix/KV caching for model key-values to speed autoregressive generation; for rerank, we cache candidate sets and embeddings at two layers: short-lived query cache and medium-term embedding cache. that reduces calls to the model by ~30-60% depending on cache TTL.
05:28 Ethan: any recommendations on batch sizing? our query distribution has many small queries and some big spikes.
05:34 Maya: dynamic batching works well — unify requests within a small time window (20-50ms) to fill a GPU batch. batching reduces per-token cost but increases latency slightly. Dedicated lets you set autoscaling thresholds to maintain latency SLOs while batching for efficiency.
05:50 Tom: about cost — can you ballpark cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our load?
05:56 Alex: rough numbers: for steady 60 QPS with top-10 rerank on GPU, Hosted may be simpler but more variable cost; Dedicated reserved capacity typically lowers unit cost by 30-50% at commit levels. exacts depend on model size and batching. we'll run estimates after you share the sample traffic.
06:15 Priya: model choices — do you recommend running the reranker as a small fine-tuned cross-encoder or using a bi-encoder + lightweight cross? what fits production best?
06:26 Maya: cross-encoder rerankers give best accuracy for top-K but are heavier. hybrid approach: use bi-encoder for initial retrieval and a distilled cross-encoder for rerank. If tail latency is critical, consider tiny cross-encoders or cascade models (cheap filter then heavy rerank only on hard cases).
06:45 Ethan: for the pilot, we'd like to test a distilled cross-encoder at 6-8B and a tiny 1-2B baseline. can Redwood host those?
06:53 Diego: yes, we support a range of model sizes and quantization—8-bit and 4-bit support on Dedicated/Private. for Hosted we have curated models; if you need custom weights in Private we can ingest them behind your network.
07:10 Priya: audit logs — we need per-call tracing back to query id, user id, and model version.
07:18 Alex: that's available — Console shows per-route traces and token-level cost, and Private can forward raw audit logs into your SIEM.
07:26 Sara: what's the uplift for compliance for Private vs Dedicated? do we need additional attestation?
07:31 Alex: Private typically meets the strictest requirements because compute and data stay in your network; Dedicated is good if you trust the provider tenancy model but want predictable capacity; Hosted requires contractual guarantees for data handling. we'll include a comparison table in follow-up.
07:50 Priya: let's talk about fallback policies — if the reranker gets overloaded do you have graceful degradation?
07:56 Maya: yes, we do automatic fallback to a lighter model or to no-rerank and serve lexical+vector results. Rollouts can be configured to fallback to a cached result set or to a cheaper model variant.
08:12 Tom: integration effort — what code changes are expected in our search stack?
08:18 Diego: minimal wrapper: after you get top-K ids from ES+Milvus, call the rerank endpoint with candidate ids and optionally full text or precomputed embeddings. we provide SDKs in Python/Go and example code for streaming and batching.
08:34 Ethan: can we send embeddings instead of text to save bandwidth?
08:37 Maya: yes, the reranker can accept embeddings and do cross-similarity scoring; sending embeddings reduces the tokenization/work on the service but requires consistent embedding model and dims.
08:48 Priya: data residency — some clients require data never leave country. can Private deploy to our regional colo?
08:54 Alex: yes, Private supports regional on-prem installs; we also offer VPC-only options for Dedicated to keep network locality.
09:03 Priya: okay, let's nail down the pilot scope. we want: accuracy baseline (recall@10, MRR), latency (p50/p95 end-to-end), cost-per-query, and failure behavior. target is p95 <250ms for rerank stage and end-to-end <400ms for UI.
09:22 Alex: that sounds good. proposed pilot: 2-week eval: week 1 dry-run with a 10k query eval set, week 2 live smoke on 10% of traffic in a canary. SEs run three configs as discussed.
09:36 Ethan: do we need to reindex embeddings for 768? can we real-time project?
09:42 Diego: you can re-embed offline; some vector DBs support on-the-fly projection but it's safer to reindex for consistent NN behavior. we can help with re-ingestion pipelines and sharding considerations.
09:56 Priya: sharding — with 12M docs, how do you recommend sharding Milvus?
10:01 Maya: shard by tenant or region; ensure each shard fits on node memory for vector lookup; horizontal scaling for fanout helps with tail latency. we'll provide recommended shard sizes based on your sample vectors.
10:18 Tom: one more on monitoring — what dashboards do you expose?
10:22 Alex: Console has per-route latency, token cost, model version per-call stats, failure rates, and sampling of request/response. you can send traces to Datadog or forward logs to your SIEM.
10:34 Sara: ok can you confirm what we get in the compliance pack? specifically: SOC2 report, data flow diagram, SAML/SCIM integration docs, KMS options, incident response SLA.
10:44 Alex: yes, we'll bundle those.
10:47 Priya: timeline — we want to decide vendor by end of August, pilot starts early September if we move forward.
10:53 Alex: that's reasonable. we'll aim to have the security pack and pricing out by next week so you can review legal and procurement.
10:59 Ethan: any gotchas on model quantization and retrieval quality we should pre-check?
11:05 Maya: yes, quantization can slightly shift neighbor distances; always validate with your recall and rerank eval. also check how your vector DB implements exact vs approximate search (HNSW params affect recall/latency).
11:18 Priya: good call. okay let's do a quick recap of next steps before we wrap.
11:23 Alex: recap: Redwood to send SOC2 + KMS docs and network diagram; SE to schedule benchmark deep dive; customer to provide anonymized dataset and success criteria; contract/pricing draft from AE. any other items?
11:40 Sara: please include pointer for per-tenant key rotation frequency and proof of HSM usage in Private.
11:45 Alex: noted.
11:47 Tom: I'll coordinate infra access for the pilot.
11:50 Priya: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
11:53 Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with materials and calendar invites.

End transcript.
